newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU aims to focus on positive in U.S. relations.
newsitem.headline: EU aims to focus on positive in U.S. relations.

text.p: Following a year of strained relations with the U.S. over trade policy, European Union foreign ministers are seeking to start 1997 on the right foot by focusing on the high points of relations with Washington.

Diplomats said a meeting of EU foreign ministers at the Genral Affairs Council in Brussels on Monday will stress the importance of maintaining good relations with Washington and repairing the cracks caused by the Helms-Burton row.
The EU was infuriated by what it saw as a rash of unacceptable extra-territorial laws emerging from Washington last year -- mainly involving trade with Cuba, Iran and Libya.

The Helms-Burton Act -- an amalgamation of decades of U.S. anti-Cuba policy -- incensed EU ministers particularly as it threatened some European companies with punitive lawsuits unless they disinvested from Cuba.

Named for its congressional sponsors, the act among other things allows naturalised Americans to sue in U.S. courts any European company or individual deemed to have benefited from investments in property confiscated by the government of Fidel Castro since the Cuban communist revolution of 1959.
The EU responded by taking a complaint to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) -- where it is now being processed -- and also by swiftly enacting laws which bar Europeans from complying with the laws.
On January 3 U.S. President Bill Clinton suspended that part of the act for six months, ostensibly as a reward to Washington's allies for helping further isolate Havana.

But the threat of court action -- and similar action from the D'Amato Bill which seeks to isolate Iran and Libya -- remains and the Netherlands, the current EU president -- is determined to push these to the backburner.

Dutch diplomats have said they will be trying to stress the positive along the lines fixed by the New Transatlantic Agenda, an agreemnent between the EU and U.S. which outlines the scope for relations.
The next EU/U.S. summit takes place in the Hague in May and the Dutch are determined this meeting will trumpet the achievements and close links between the world's two biggest trading partners.

These include negotiations on mutual recognition agreements, the finalisation of an information technology agreement and the completion of a basic telecoms trade deal currently being negotiated at the WTO in Geneva.
Ministers will also on Monday highlight the growing political cooperation bweteen the EU and Washington -- particularly in sensitive areas such as the Middle East and former Yugoslavia.
Monday's meeting will also review last month's signing of a cooperation agreement with Canada which covers foreign policy, security, economic and commercial links.

Also on the agenda is the situation in the Great Lakes region of Africa, the Middle East, results of the WTO ministerial meeting in Singapore last year, the situation in Belarus and in former Yugoslavia.
